title: Using Spies
note: He says this means employing spies to learn what happens among enemies, neutrals and friends. A ruler needs it both to run his own land and to take others’, so it comes first.

couplets.plain: Spies and books of high repute: a ruler should be clear that these two are his eyes.
couplets.pm: A ruler should settle on spies and the renowned books of statecraft as his two eyes. Spies go through all the expanse his own eyes can’t reach and report what happened. The books tell him what to do about it, where his own understanding can’t reach. They are his eye of flesh and his eye of wisdom.

links.quote: Spies and books of high repute
links.reason: Gives spies equal place with the renowned books as what a ruler sees by.

links.quote: a ruler should be clear
links.reason: Speaks by name to the ruler about what he must take as his eyes.

links.quote: these two are his eyes

couplets.plain: To know quickly, every day, all that happens to everyone is a ruler’s work.
couplets.pm: A ruler’s proper work is to learn quickly through spies, every day, everything that happens among all people, whether enemies, neutrals or friends: good and bad words and deeds alike. He must know at once, so that he can show favour or punish as each deserves.

links.quote: a ruler’s work
links.reason: Makes knowing at once what happens to everyone the ruler’s stated work.

links.quote: To know quickly, every day, all that happens to everyone
links.reason: Knowing all that happens to everyone, every day, is what a ruler’s spies are for.

couplets.plain: A ruler who doesn’t spy through his spies and weigh what they find has no road to victory.
couplets.pm: A ruler who doesn’t have spies watch what happens among all people, and doesn’t weigh what can be gained from it, has no other road to victory. Knowing neither, he lies open to his enemies, and nothing else can cure that. He allows the reading “there is no victory for him to win” as well.

links.quote: doesn’t spy through his spies
links.reason: Rules out victory for the ruler who doesn’t spy through his spies.

links.quote: A ruler who doesn’t spy

couplets.plain: A spy is someone who watches everyone alike: those who do your work, your own kin, and those who wish you ill.
couplets.pm: A spy is the one who examines, through their words and deeds, all those who do the ruler’s work, his kin and his enemies. The ruler must know what his workers do, what his kin do to him and his land, and how his enemies probe his weak moments. So none of the three may be left out.

links.quote: watches everyone alike
those who do your work, your own kin
links.reason: The work, the kin and the enemies are the ruler’s own, so this account of a spy is meant for him.

links.quote: those who do your work
links.reason: Names those who do the ruler’s work first among those to be watched.

couplets.plain: A spy is someone with a look that draws no suspicion, who doesn’t flinch under a stare, and who never lets anything spill.
couplets.pm: A spy is one who takes a form the people he watches won’t suspect, such as a Brahmin’s or a merchant’s. If they do grow suspicious he doesn’t fear their angry stare, and whichever of the four means they try on him, he doesn’t spit out what is in his mind.

links.quote: A spy is someone with a look that draws no suspicion
never lets anything spill

couplets.plain: A spy takes the form of those who have renounced, goes where others can’t and searches, and gives nothing away, whatever is done to them.
couplets.pm: A spy keeps the vows of those who have wholly renounced, such as pilgrimage to sacred waters, gets into every place hard to enter and finds out what he must. People seldom harm one they take for holy, but even if they suspect him, seize him and torture him, he doesn’t reveal himself. Some take படிவம் as only a disguise.
couplets.note: படிவம் can mean a form or a vow. The plain reading takes form. He takes vow.

links.quote: the form of those who have renounced
links.reason: Has the spy go about in the form of those who have renounced.

links.quote: gives nothing away, whatever is done to them

couplets.plain: A spy is someone who can hear what has been hidden, and has no doubt about what they have learned.
couplets.pm: A spy can hear what those he watches did in secret, from people close to them, and then settle on what he heard without doubt. He finds who knows, gets near without raising suspicion, leads them on with fitting words and deeds until they tell it themselves, and listens as if it were nothing to him. If he reports with doubts, the ruler can’t act.

links.quote: can hear what has been hidden
links.reason: Picks out two skills: hearing what is hidden and being sure of what was learned.

couplets.plain: What one spy has spied out and brought you, have another spy find out too.
couplets.pm: Have what one spy has found and reported spied out by another spy as well, and see whether the two match. A spy may side with those he watches and report falsely, so one man’s word can’t be trusted.

links.quote: have another spy find out too

couplets.plain: Use spies so that one spy doesn’t know another. When three agree, believe it.
couplets.pm: Employ spies so that none knows another. Send three such spies on one matter, and if what all three say agrees in substance, trust it as true. Spies who knew each other would agree among themselves. Three can’t easily become of one mind, or stay so. If their words don’t agree, look further.

links.quote: When three agree, believe it
Use spies so that one spy doesn’t know another

couplets.plain: Don’t honour a spy where others can see. If you do, you have brought your own secret out into the open.
couplets.pm: A ruler shouldn’t honour a spy who has reported hidden things where others can know of it. If he does, he himself throws out the secret he should keep: that the man is a spy, and what he said. People will ask who this man is and why he was honoured, and those who ask and answer are outsiders.

links.quote: brought your own secret out into the open
Don’t honour a spy
links.reason: The spy here is his own, so the one addressed is the ruler who employs him.
